name: Nemean Lion
body:
Nemean Lion
CR 7/MR 2

This giant cat’s mane and tawny coat glisten golden, while it flexes its powerful limbs and roars thunderously, ready to leap to attack.

XP 2,400
N Large magical beast (mythic)
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +16; Aura frightful presence (60 ft., DC 16)

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 13, flat-footed 15 (+4 Dex, +6 natural, -1 size)
hp 86 (7d10+48)
Fort +10, Ref +10, Will +5
Defensive Abilities immortal spark, impenetrable hide; DR 10/bludgeoning and 5/epic; Immune fear

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee bite +14 (2d6+7 plus grab), 2 claws +13 (1d6+7)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 10 ft.
Special Attacks mythic power (2/day, surge +1d6), piercing fang and claw, pounce, rake (2 claws +13, 1d6+7)

STATISTICS

Str 25, Dex 19, Con 18, Int 12, Wis 16, Cha 17
Base Atk +7; CMB +15 (+19 grapple); CMD 29 (33 vs. trip)
Feats Improved Natural Attack (bite), RunMF, Skill Focus (Perception), Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Acrobatics +18 (+30 running jump), Perception +16, Stealth +14 (+18 in undergrowth); Racial Modifiers +4 Acrobatics (+16 running jump), +4 Stealth (+8 in undergrowth)
Languages Common (cannot speak)

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Immortal Spark (Ex)

A Nemean lion is immune to death effects and cannot die of old age.

It doesn’t take penalties to its ability scores for aging and cannot be magically aged.

Impenetrable Hide (Ex)

A Nemean lion’s skin cannot be pierced or cut by anything except its own claws. It is immune to bleed damage, blood drain, and critical hits or precision damage from piercing or slashing weapons. Effects that normally bypass or ignore damage reduction (like a paladin’s smite evil or a mythic champion’s fleet charge) do not bypass a nemean’s damage reduction.

Piercing Fang and Claw (Ex)

A nemean’s teeth and claws are considered epic, magical, adamantine weapons for the purpose of bypassing damage reduction.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm plains or hills
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental

The nemean is a massive lion of tremendous strength and ferocity. Though their tawny fur and flowing mane looks the same as any lion’s, it is incredibly tough and almost impossible to pierce with mortal blades. It is said the first nemean created (or cursed) by the gods had skin so impervious to blades that nothing but its own claws could cut it. The nemeans still existing in the world are not quite so invulnerable, but even so only weapons forged from truly legendary material and blessed with enchantment have any hope of shedding even a drop of its blood.

Unlike ordinary lions, they tend to be solitary, only rarely seeking the company of other felines. If they encounter an existing pride, they swiftly dispatch all rivals and dominate the survivors until they tire of their company and move on.

They are loathe to let others hunt for them, preferring the thrill of the chase and the glory of the kill with their own jaws.

As a rule, nemeans live in solitary places and don’t meddle with humanoids or other sentient races, though an old specimen can become violent and attack people if it has lost its pride and is left to defend its territory alone. Sometimes, these mythic beasts can also be sent by powerful entities to haunt a definite region or assigned to guard a prohibited land or treasure. Powerful adventurers search Nemean lions for their coat, which can be made into hide armor with the impervious or invulnerable qualities.
